title: Lead coaching sync — API/Console/Dedicated/Private — quick jotter
content:
Context: weekly coach-style 1:1 with Alex (eng lead - Console & API surfaces). Goal = unblock Dedicated capacity contract discussions, confirm canary rollout schedule for console routing changes, and align on Private packaging timeline that sales keeps asking about. Quick, tactical + some career/coaching items squeezed in.

Topline to start (2 min):
- Dedicated negotiating: legal wants clearer SLAs for regional failover, finance pushing for a 6-month ramp commitment instead of 12. We need an ops-cost estimate for 6mo vs 12mo.
- Console canary: small subset (10% orgs) to be routed to new policy engine starting next Tue. Need final fallback metric and abort criteria.
- Private: last QA revealed installer race on postgres init; delays packaging by ~2 weeks if we don't triage.

Agenda (30 min total)
1) Quick status (5m) — what changed since last time?
2) Dedicated commercial ask (8m) — numbers needed, risk profile, fallback options
3) Console canary readiness (8m) — abort criteria, monitoring, runbook owners
4) Private packaging triage (6m) — blocker plan, release freeze window
5) Coaching/people (3m) — Alex ask + calibration

Detailed talking points / prep notes
- Dedicated capacity negotiation
  - What we need to bring: 30/90/365 day unit cost delta (GPU hrs, pre-emptible vs reserved), expected throughput delta per pool type, and a clear customer-impact statement for ramp (if we limit burst, what SLOs degrade?).
  - Data sources: Billing analytics dashboard -> 'dedicated-commit-explorer' (Arjun owns), infra cost model PR (#4287) has opportunity/caveat notes.
  - Proposed options to present to finance/legal: 6-month with higher unit cost + auto-extension clause OR 12-month with discount + staged ramp. Need numbers this week.
  - Quick ask for Alex: can infra estimate worst-case ops delta by EOD Thursday? If not, call for a conservative guardrail we can promise.

- Console canary (routing change)
  - Canary plan: 10% orgs -> new policy engine; 24h health check window then gradual to 50% over 72h. Abort if p99 tokens latency increases > 25% over baseline or error-rate > 0.5% for more than 15m.
  - Monitoring: dashboards (console/routing/p99-tokens, console/error-rate), synthetic checks every minute from three regions. We need someone on-call for first 48h (signup sheet?).
  - Runbook: rollback via flag flip (feature-flag-service). Confirmed with release-engineering but need to rehearse if flag flip is not instantaneous under load.
  - Items to push on: make abort criteria explicit in the canary announcement (so sales/customer success know how to interpret). Also note that some customers have custom routing rules — add them to the exclude list.

- Private deployment package
  - Issue: postgres-init race discovered by QA — manifest: init script sometimes double-writes schema version causing bootstrap failure. Repro rate ~1-in-30 deploys in test harness.
  - Quick triage path: Alex to assign an engineer to reproduce deterministically with trace logs; if can't reproduce, revert to slower init sequence for RC build.
  - Impact: delays 'private-1.3' release by ~2 weeks unless fast patch. Sales mentioned two on-prem pilots target launch end of March — flag as high priority.

Open questions to surface in the meeting
- Are we comfortable committing to a 6-month dedicated contract publicly as an option? (trade: shorter commitment -> higher unit price; we need to bake guardrails)
- Can SRE guarantee a rollback under heavy load within 5m? (if not, change abort thresholds)
- Who owns customer comms for canary aborts? (product or CS?)

Decisions I want us to make in the meeting
- Pick one of the two Dedicated billing options to take to finance by Friday.
- Lock abort criteria for console canary and identify on-call for first 48h.
- Agree to an emergency private RC plan (patch vs slow-init fallback) and set release freeze window.

Data to bring / attach during meeting
- p99 latency baseline last 7 days (api/console) — screenshot from dashboard or copy numeric table.
- Cost delta sketch from infra cost model PR #4287 (summary note).
- QA run logs showing postgres-init failure (link to S3 artifacts).

Action items (post-meeting template)
- Alex: get worst-case ops delta estimate for 6mo vs 12mo (due Thu EOD).
- Arjun: export dedicated billing delta table and add notes to PR #4287 (due Wed).
- Me (Megan): draft the finance/legal one-pager showing the two options + recommended ask (due Fri noon).
- SRE/Release Eng (TBD): assign on-call coverage for canary first 48h; share signup link in #console-release (due Mon).
- Alex + QA: reproduce postgres-init failure and either commit patch or enable slow-init RC (decision by next Wed).

Notes-to-self (prep mental checklist)
- Start meeting with a 60s framing to avoid getting stuck in technical minutiae.
- If Alex pushes for 'no 6-month', ask for a concrete alternative with numbers.
- Keep coaching segment short — ask Alex about direct report ramp and one decision he needs my unblock on.

Parking lot / follow-ups to handle later
- Longer discussion on routing policies for multi-tenant noisy neighbors (schedule separate deep dive: invite SRE + infra).
- Revisit Dedicated pricing templates for sales collateral (owner: revenue ops).

Quick personal reflection
- Alex has been terse — might be bandwidth. Pairing on the ops delta estimate could both unblock and be a good 1:1 barbell (help and trust).

Fragments / quick stubs to paste in meeting notes if needed:
- "Abort if p99 > 125% baseline for 15m AND error-rate > 0.5%"
- "Offer A: 6mo ramp, +12% unit price, auto-ext unless cancelled 30d"
- "Offer B: 12mo commit, -8% unit price, staged ramp schedule"

End.
